private_note: I can't estimate my odds, and the plan lasts a generation with no second chance, so I'm guarding against the worst case. Hazel gives the lowest group the highest income of any plan, 41 against 15 under Cedar. Ending up at the bottom under Cedar would be ruinous, while losing the top under Hazel still leaves me comfortable. Alder is my fallback if Hazel can't reach 9 votes, because it clearly beats Today for the bottom group.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows where we will land, and nobody can tell us the odds. Whatever we pick binds us for a generation. So I asked one question: if I turn out to be in the lowest fifth, which plan treats me best? Hazel does, at 41 thousand. Under Cedar I would get 15 thousand and buy my own health coverage. Hazel was set up for exactly this purpose: it lifts the bottom as far as it can go without shrinking the economy. If I end up at the top under Hazel, I still have 159 thousand, which is a good life. If I end up at the bottom under Cedar, I don't. Each of you faces the same gamble I do. I rank Hazel first, then Birch, then Alder, and I would rather keep today's arrangements than adopt Cedar. If Hazel can't reach nine votes, I'm open to Alder as common ground.
